blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for society
to axe something is to kill it off

explanation.surface: A club or society has sacked its specialist adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axed' reads as dismissed from a job, but here it is the slang sense of finished off, cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person with great ability gained through training and practice, so the adjectives are synonyms.

blocks.note: first meaning: roguish, behaving like a rascal
second meaning: in a playing-card deck the jack is also called the knave, so like him is knave-ish

explanation.walkthrough: The jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave; the question mark flags this playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest rogue, so knavish behaviour is roguish, mischievous and tricky in nature.

indicators.note: going without something means doing without it, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: to set off a rocket or venture is to launch it
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone heads off on a journey without having eaten anything first.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from LAUNCH and LUNCH is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is a specific example of a meal, taken around noon between breakfast and dinner.

clue.text: This animal can hide in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise alters the appearance of something, so these letters are rearranged into a new look

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A creature that is able to conceal itself by camouflage.
explanation.walkthrough: The echidna, a spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea, really does hide by burrowing, so the surface fits the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal, so it is a particular example of an animal.

blocks.note: jam is a fruit preserve
a carton is a pack, as of juice or cigarettes

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep a box for filling up with goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb meaning keep, but it is the noun for fruit spread.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram a space with as much as it will hold is to stuff it completely, crowding every corner.

clue.text: Notice about pig on the bus

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a notice in a paper is an advertisement, AD for short
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A sign complaining about a pig riding on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as a verb, see, but it is the noun for a small advertisement; 'about' then wraps it round the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a vehicle means being carried as a passenger inside it, here on a bus.

clue.text: In turn quickly rue tiptoe manoeuvre

indicators.note: to manoeuvre things is to shift them around skilfully, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dancer moves on tiptoe and spins fast, then regrets the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre' reads as a noun in the dance, but it is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet spin on one foot, and as a verb it means to whirl round rapidly.

clue.text: One who has more responsibility in the navy than in the army

definitions.text: One who has more responsibility in the navy than in the army

blocks.clueFragment: One who has more responsibility in the navy than in the army
blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose job is bigger at sea than on land

blocks.clueFragment: One who has more responsibility in the navy than in the army
blocks.note: setter's reading: a rank with the same name in both services, which commands a whole ship at sea but only a company ashore

explanation.walkthrough: The same title is used in both services, but at sea it is a senior rank commanding a ship, while in the army it is a junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes an officer rank whose seniority differs between the services, which fits this title exactly.

blocks.note: someone not well is ill
to treat a subject is to consider it

explanation.surface: A skin rash that a doctor has not dealt with properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like the skin complaint, with 'treated' as medical care; both words switch sense, to hasty and to thought about.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is made hastily without enough thought, which is exactly a poorly thought-out one.

clue.text: Man who will change sex if promoted

definitions.text: Man who will change sex if promoted

blocks.clueFragment: Man who will change sex if promoted
blocks.note: surface reading: a male employee who would become female on promotion

blocks.clueFragment: Man who will change sex if promoted
blocks.note: setter's reading: a chess man that, reaching the far rank, is usually promoted to a queen

explanation.walkthrough: In chess the pieces are called men; the lowliest one, on reaching the last rank, is promoted and normally becomes a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The humblest chess piece is a man that can be promoted to queen, the only female piece on the board.

clue.text: In hole I repot flourishing plant

indicators.note: something flourishing is waved about with a flourish, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener repots a thriving plant into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourishing' looks like it describes the healthy plant, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden shrub with fragrant purple flowers, so it is a particular kind of plant.

indicators.note: reporters take down what they hear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a team is a side, as in a football side

explanation.surface: A team tells the press how let down they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To reporters' sounds like the audience for a statement, but it signals that we hear the word for team.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long audible breath that typically shows sadness or being let down.

clue.text: Sort of saw letter being passed round

blocks.note: first meaning: a power saw with a spinning toothed disc
second meaning: a notice sent round to many people

explanation.surface: Someone glimpsed a note that was going round the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see, but it is the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular saw has a round blade, and a circular is a letter copied and distributed widely.

indicators.note: toying means playing about idly, so these letters are played with into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Lively Pam is fiddling with the coins in her pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like an adjective describing Pam, but it is the noun for sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is informal slang for sparkling wine, especially the famous French one from Reims and Épernay.

clue.text: Forecasters got together away from freezing conditions

blocks.note: people who got together met
off means away from
ice forms in freezing conditions

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters held a meeting somewhere warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national weather service employs meteorologists who produce weather forecasts, so it stands for forecasters collectively.

clue.text: Special aquarium betrayed lack of cleaning?

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for special
a fish tank is an aquarium

explanation.surface: A special fish tank revealed that nobody had cleaned it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful, hence the question mark: something that smelled foul gave away that it had not been washed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad smell is evidence of dirt, so smelling bad gave away the neglect of washing.

blocks.note: to spit is to eject from the mouth forcefully
in algebra unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: Someone violently throws out a stray dog nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians call unknown quantities x, y and z, so 'unknown' can give any of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The spitz is a breed type of dog with a pointed muzzle and curled tail, such as the Pomeranian.

indicators.note: when something opens up it splits to let something inside it

blocks.note: too means also
a plan is a map, as of a building

explanation.surface: A military unit is also unfolding its map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as the act of unfolding the map, but it means the map splits apart to take the other word in.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of an army company, a small unit of soldiers under a lieutenant.

blocks.note: DIs are detective inspectors
if you will is a polite request, as is please

explanation.surface: A polite invitation to irritate the police.
explanation.walkthrough: DI stands for Detective Inspector, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to irritate them or make them unhappy, so the two verbs are synonyms.

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of publicity for a product
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone wires up an advert the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break moves: PLUG plus SIN regroups as PLUGS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugging in an appliance attaches it to the electricity supply, linking it to the mains.

clue.text: Small job for gardener, and one for farrier

definitions.note: 'one' stands for a job, so this means a farrier's job

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
gardeners hoe weeds

explanation.surface: A list of tasks for two tradesmen, one in the garden and one at the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: A farrier fits horseshoes; adding S to the gardener's task gives the farrier's.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier's main work is fitting iron plates to horses' hooves, so that task is his job.

clue.text: Regularly moving parts of railway line

definitions.text: Regularly moving parts of railway line

blocks.clueFragment: Regularly moving parts of railway line
blocks.note: surface reading: any components of a track that shift often

blocks.clueFragment: Regularly moving parts of railway line
blocks.note: setter's reading: the movable rails at a junction that switch trains from one track to another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' hints at alternate letters, but no fodder gives the answer; the clue simply describes the movable rails at a junction, called switches in America.
explanation.definitionFit: On British railways the movable tapered rails that divert trains between tracks are known by this name.

clue.text: Immature feelings for one of the herd?

blocks.note: first meaning: a youthful infatuation, puppy love
second meaning, taken literally: affection for a young cow

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a young bovine in the herd as the object of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a teenager's short-lived romantic crush, much like puppy love.

blocks.note: lifts are ups, as in ups and downs
very warm is hot

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the elevators are overheated, then celebrates a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result!' looks like a cry of triumph, but it is the plain noun for an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of events is their final outcome or consequence, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Little furry animal wild in Basle

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; Basle is the Swiss city of Basel

explanation.surface: A small furry creature living in the wild near Basel in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like it describes the animal, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The sable is a small marten-like mammal of Siberia prized for its soft dark fur.

indicators.note: to be without a leader is to lose the one at the front, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: a deadpan face shows no feeling

explanation.surface: A comedian keeps a straight face, even with nobody in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb meaning even so, but it is the adjective for unmoving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is not moving at all, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone judges an inducement to be slightly improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit off' reads as the British phrase for rather unfair, but it splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is food used to lure fish or animals, and figuratively any lure or temptation.

definitions.note: describes something written as poetry, the opposite of prose

blocks.note: first meaning: the reverse or contrary of something
second meaning, split in two: the opposite of written in prose is written in poetry

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as IN VERSE: the opposite of prosaic (literally, in prose) is written as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The inverse of something is its reverse or contrary, and in verse means in poetic form.

clue.text: Don’t travel far enough to suffer?

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: to go short of the distance is to go under it
second meaning: to endure or experience something unpleasant

explanation.surface: Advice that a trip too short will cause hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UNDER-GO: to fall short of a target is to undergo it in this fanciful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo an operation or ordeal is to experience and endure it, so it means suffer.
